transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you here today?

Mostly I came in because I’m just… tired. And I don’t mean the normal kind where you stay up too late or have a rough week and then catch up on sleep. I mean I can sleep, get up, go to work, do what I’m supposed to do, and still feel like I’m starting the day with the battery already half-drained—or lower than that, honestly.

I manage computer systems for work, so I’m used to pushing through and keeping things running, and I can still do that. It’s not like I’ve completely fallen apart or anything. But it feels harder than it should. Like before the day even really gets going, I’m already dragging, and I find myself wondering why I feel so worn down when, on paper, I should be okay. That’s the part that finally made me think I should come talk to someone, because it doesn’t make much sense to me.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that activities you once looked forward to now feel like a chore or don’t interest you anymore?

Yeah… yes, I have noticed that. It’s not that I can’t do anything, exactly. I still go through the motions, and sometimes I’ll even make myself do the things I used to like because I think, well, maybe if I just get out there it’ll feel the way it used to. But a lot of the time it just doesn’t.

Like fishing, for example. I used to really look forward to that—getting my gear together, being out by the water, the quiet of it. Now it can feel like another thing I’m supposed to do, like I’m checking a box that says “do something enjoyable.” Same with tending the tomatoes. I’ll water them, pull weeds, look them over, but there isn’t much satisfaction in it. Even something simple like a church concert, where I used to enjoy the music and seeing people, now I might go and sit there, but it feels kind of flat.

It’s been that way for a long time, honestly. Most days there’s just this gray feeling over things. Not dramatic, not like I’m breaking down, but like the color’s been turned down on everything. Things I used to look forward to don’t really pull me in anymore. They just feel like part of the list.
Do you find yourself feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes… I think that’s a fair way to put it. Most days, there’s this kind of gray, flat feeling that’s just there in the background. It’s not always me sitting there crying or anything like that, so for a long time I didn’t really call it “depressed,” exactly. I’d just think, well, I’m tired, or it’s been a long week, or I’m getting older, or work is work.

But when I’m honest about it, yeah, it’s there most of the day on a lot of days. Things feel muted. Like I can go fishing or tend the tomatoes or go to a church concert, and from the outside it looks like I’m doing normal things I used to enjoy, but inside it feels more like I’m checking off a list than actually looking forward to it or taking much pleasure in it. It’s just sort of… flat. Like there’s a dullness over everything that doesn’t really lift much.
Have you found yourself feeling like you’re not good enough, or blamed yourself for things more than you normally would?

I don’t know that I’d put it that way, exactly. I mean, I can be hard on myself sometimes, but I’ve always had a bit of that—especially with work, if something doesn’t go smoothly, I’ll replay it and think about what I should’ve caught sooner or handled better. But I’m not sure it’s more than normal for me.

I wouldn’t say I walk around feeling like I’m worthless or anything like that. It’s more… I get frustrated with myself for not having more energy, or for not enjoying things the way I think I should. Sometimes I’ll think, “What’s wrong with me? Other people seem to just get on with it.” But I don’t know if that’s blaming myself so much as being confused by it.

So… maybe a little self-critical, yes, but not in some constant, heavy way where I feel like I’m not good enough all the time. It’s not the main thing I’ve noticed.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough or that you’re failing others, even when things are going okay?

Not really, no. I mean… I can have those thoughts in passing, like anybody, I suppose. If something at work is messy or I forget to follow up on something, I’ll think, “Well, you should’ve handled that better.” But I don’t think I’m walking around with a strong feeling that I’m failing people or that I’m not good enough.

It’s more like I get irritated with myself sometimes—especially when I’m not as engaged as I think I should be, or when something that ought to feel satisfying just doesn’t. But I don’t usually turn that into, “I’m a failure,” if that makes sense. I don’t feel like I’m constantly letting everyone down, or that things are going fine and I still believe I’m somehow ruining them.

So… I’d say no, not in any big or regular way. Maybe some self-criticism here and there, but not that deeper feeling of not being good enough.
Do you feel like you have less energy than usual or find yourself feeling fatigued, even after resting or sleeping?

Yes, that’s actually one of the main reasons I came in. I’m tired in a way that doesn’t really add up to me.

I mean, I can sleep. It’s not like I’m staying up all night every night or anything like that. And I’m still getting myself to work, still doing what I need to do, managing the day-to-day things. From the outside I probably look like I’m functioning okay. But inside it feels like I’m starting the day with the battery already half-drained, or lower than that sometimes.

Even after resting, I don’t really feel refreshed the way I think I should. I’ll think, “Well, maybe if I just take it easy tonight,” or “Maybe after the weekend I’ll feel caught up,” but then the morning comes and it’s like I’m already running on low before I’ve even really begun. It’s not dramatic, exactly—I’m not collapsing or unable to move around—but it’s this steady tiredness that follows me around and makes everything take more effort than it seems like it should.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or thinking clearly lately, like it's harder to focus or make decisions than it used to be?

I don’t think so, not in any major way. I mean, I’m 63, so I’m not going to pretend I never walk into a room and forget why I went in there, or have to reread an email because I skimmed it the first time. But that doesn’t feel new or especially alarming to me.

At work, I’m still able to follow what’s going on, make decisions, keep track of things. Sometimes I feel a little slower getting started or I’ll put off making a small decision because I just don’t feel like dealing with it right then, but once I sit down and focus, I can usually do it. It’s not like my mind goes blank or I can’t think clearly.

So… I wouldn’t say concentration is the big issue. Maybe I’m not as sharp when I’m worn out, but I haven’t noticed some clear change where I can’t focus or make decisions the way I used to.
Do you find that you take less pleasure in things overall, even when you're able to do them?

Yes… yes, I do. That’s probably the part that bothers me the most, if I’m being honest, because it’s not that I can’t do things. I can still go through the motions. I’ll go fishing if I said I would, or I’ll tend to the tomatoes, or go to a church concert if there’s one I would normally have liked. But it all has this kind of gray, flat feeling over it.

It’s like the enjoyment doesn’t really arrive. I’ll be there, doing the thing, and some part of me knows, “You used to look forward to this. This used to feel good.” But now it can feel more like another item on a checklist—go here, do that, keep up with the garden, attend the concert—rather than something I’m actually taking pleasure in.

And it’s been that way for a long time, not just a bad week or two. Most days there’s this dullness to things. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, like I’m completely unable to enjoy anything at all, but overall, yes, things feel muted. Like the color’s been turned down.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in almost everything, even things you used to really enjoy?

Almost everything… I’d say most things, yes. Maybe not every single thing without exception, but enough that it feels like it’s spread over my whole life.

For a long time now there’s been this gray, flat feeling most days. Things I used to genuinely look forward to—going fishing, tending the tomatoes, going to a church concert—now I still do them sometimes, but they don’t land the same way. It’s more like, “Okay, I said I’d go fishing, so I’ll go,” or “The tomatoes need attention, so I’ll go out and do that,” or “There’s a concert, and I would normally attend, so I’ll show up.” But it feels more like checking something off a list than actually enjoying it.

And that’s hard to explain because I’m not sitting there thinking I hate these things. I don’t hate them. I just don’t feel much from them. It’s like I remember that I used to enjoy them more than I actually enjoy them now.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that even small tasks take a lot more effort to get started?

I don’t know if I’d say I’m visibly moving slower, like someone watching me would necessarily notice it. I still get up, get dressed, get to work, do what needs doing. But small tasks… yes, they can feel like they take more effort to get started than they ought to.

Mostly what made me come in is that I’m tired in a way that doesn’t really make sense to me. I can sleep, I can keep up at work, I can get through the day, but I still feel like I’m running on a low battery before the day has even really gotten going. It’s not that I’m collapsing or unable to function, but there’s this heaviness to starting things—answering a message, taking care of something around the house, even just getting myself moving in the morning.

Once I’m into something, I can usually keep going. But getting over that first little hump feels harder than it should. It’s like everything requires an extra push that I don’t remember needing before.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty about things you've done, or like you're a burden to others, even when there's no clear reason for it?

I don’t think so… not in that way, at least. I mean, I can second-guess myself like anybody, and I’ll worry if I’ve let someone down or if I didn’t handle something as well as I could have. But I wouldn’t say I’m walking around feeling guilty for no clear reason, or like I’m some big burden on everyone.

Sometimes I might feel bad if I’m not as cheerful or engaged as people expect me to be, but that’s more… I don’t know, more frustration with myself than guilt, maybe. I still try to carry my weight and not make my mood other people’s problem.

So, no, I haven’t really noticed a strong feeling of guilt or feeling like I’m a burden. That doesn’t feel like the main thing for me.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, or do you still have some interest, even if it doesn’t feel as strong as it used to?

I wouldn’t say completely, no. That’s maybe the strange part of it. I still have some interest, at least in the sense that I remember those things matter to me, and I still go through the motions of doing them.

Like fishing, for example—I can still decide to go, get the gear together, be out there by the water, and part of me knows, “This is something I used to really look forward to.” Same with tending the tomatoes, or going to a church concert. I still show up for those things sometimes. It’s not like I’ve rejected them or they mean nothing at all.

But for a long time now, there’s been this gray, flat feeling most days. The enjoyment just doesn’t come through the way it used to. It’s more like those things have turned into items on a checklist—go fishing because I said I would, take care of the tomatoes because they need tending, attend the concert because that’s what I would normally do. I’m doing the same activities, but the feeling behind them is muted.

So I guess the answer is: I still have some interest, but it’s weaker. Much weaker than it used to be.

It’s not that I’m collapsing or unable to function, but there’s this heaviness to starting things—answering a message, taking care of something around the house, even just getting myself moving in the morning.

Once I’m into something, I can usually keep going. But getting over that first little hump feels harder than it should. It’s like everything requires an extra push that I don’t remember needing before.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, which could help differentiate between major depressive disorder and other conditions.
doctor.question: Have you found yourself feeling guilty about things you've done, or like you're a burden to others, even when there's no clear reason for it?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about excessive guilt or feeling like a burden, and the provided symptom profile does not include a guilt/worthlessness symptom item.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not in that way, at least. I mean, I can second-guess myself like anybody, and I’ll worry if I’ve let someone down or if I didn’t handle something as well as I could have. But I wouldn’t say I’m walking around feeling guilty for no clear reason, or like I’m some big burden on everyone.

Sometimes I might feel bad if I’m not as cheerful or engaged as people expect me to be, but that’s more… I don’t know, more frustration with myself than guilt, maybe. I still try to carry my weight and not make my mood other people’s problem.

So, no, I haven’t really noticed a strong feeling of guilt or feeling like I’m a burden. That doesn’t feel like the main thing for me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant loss of interest or pleasure in activities, which would help differentiate between major depressive disorder and other depressive disorders.
doctor.question: Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, or do you still have some interest, even if it doesn’t feel as strong as it used to?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: For a long time now there’s been this gray, flat feeling most days, where even things I used to look forward to like fishing, tending the tomatoes, or a church concert feel like items on a checklist instead of something I enjoy.
target_item.reason: The question is directly about reduced interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities, which is covered by the Depressed_Mood profile manifestation describing enjoyable activities feeling flat or like checklist items.

patient.answer:
I wouldn’t say completely, no. That’s maybe the strange part of it. I still have some interest, at least in the sense that I remember those things matter to me, and I still go through the motions of doing them.

Like fishing, for example—I can still decide to go, get the gear together, be out there by the water, and part of me knows, “This is something I used to really look forward to.” Same with tending the tomatoes, or going to a church concert. I still show up for those things sometimes. It’s not like I’ve rejected them or they mean nothing at all.

But for a long time now, there’s been this gray, flat feeling most days. The enjoyment just doesn’t come through the way it used to. It’s more like those things have turned into items on a checklist—go fishing because I said I would, take care of the tomatoes because they need tending, attend the concert because that’s what I would normally do. I’m doing the same activities, but the feeling behind them is muted.

So I guess the answer is: I still have some interest, but it’s weaker. Much weaker than it used to be.
